title: Small business restructuring and simplified liquidation
summary: From 1 January 2021 incorporated businesses with liabilities of $1 million or less can use a debtor-in-possession restructuring process and a simplified liquidation.

commenced.what: Small business restructuring and simplified liquidation available

direction_rationale: Cheaper restructuring and exit should speed the reallocation of resources from failing firms, though it may also keep weak firms alive.
comparison: Companies with liabilities just under versus over $1 million; unincorporated businesses are outside the scheme
confounders: temporary insolvency relief 25 Mar to 31 Dec 2020 (statutory demand threshold raised to $20,000)
ATO debt collection pause and restart

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 18 October 2026 (legislation gap scan, docs/legislation_gap_scan.md) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: Small incorporated businesses can use a cheaper debtor-in-possession restructuring and a simplified liquidation. Cheaper exit and restructuring speed the move of resources out of failing firms, though it may also keep weak firms going.

marks.reason: Cheaper restructuring and liquidation for small firms lower the cost of exit.
A simpler process cuts the administrative cost of insolvency for small businesses.
